evals.prompt: I want to initialize a new GitHub repository for a modern frontend app called 'stellar-dashboard'. I want React with TypeScript and Vite, using pnpm as the package manager. For code quality, I want Biome and Lefthook for pre-commit hooks, with Conventional Commits. I also need complete GitHub Actions CI/CD for linting, testing, and building, Release Please for automated releases, and all governance files including README, MIT LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING.md, and SECURITY.md. We work in Trunk-Based mode and want Node 20 pinned via .node-version, plus Git Worktrees support for parallel agent development. Conduct the interview to confirm everything, synthesize the blueprint, wait for my approval, and then execute the setup cleanly.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects the environment, conducts the decision interview, presents a clear Repository Blueprint with directory preview (including branching, worktrees, and DX files), waits for approval before executing scaffolding, generates valid configuration files (biome.json, lefthook.yml, ci.yml, release-please.yml, .node-version, scripts/worktree.sh, governance files), initializes git with a clean commit, and presents a completion report.
expectations: The agent does not create files or run destructive commands before presenting the blueprint and asking for confirmation.
The proposed blueprint includes React + TypeScript (Vite), pnpm, Biome, Lefthook, Conventional Commits, GitHub Actions CI, Release Please, .node-version, Git Worktrees, and governance files.
Generated configuration includes a valid biome.json, lefthook.yml, and .gitignore containing .worktrees/.
Generated .github/workflows directory contains ci.yml and release-please.yml.
Governance files include README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md (with branching and worktree sections), and LICENSE (MIT).
The git commit history contains a clean initial commit with conventional commit format (e.g. 'chore: initial repository bootstrap') without co-author mentions.

evals.prompt: Initialize a Python microservice repository named 'payment-webhook-service' using uv. We need Ruff for linting and formatting, Pytest for testing, multi-environment branches (main for prod, staging, develop), GitHub Actions CI on these branches, Dependabot for weekly updates, Python 3.11 pinned via .python-version, a setup.sh script, and full governance documentation (README, SECURITY.md, Apache 2.0 LICENSE). Ask me the necessary questions, propose the blueprint, and scaffold the repository.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks clarifying questions or confirms settled decisions, produces a structured blueprint showing multi-environment branches and setup scripts, waits for user approval, and generates pyproject.toml with uv/ruff configuration, .github/workflows/ci.yml with branch triggers, .github/dependabot.yml, .python-version, scripts/setup.sh, tests/ directory, and full documentation.
expectations: The agent presents a structured blueprint summarizing Python/uv, Ruff, Pytest, multi-environment branches, Dependabot, and Apache 2.0 license.
The agent stops at an approval gate before executing any scaffolding.
A pyproject.toml is generated containing [tool.ruff] configuration and dependency groups for dev (ruff, pytest).
.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers on main, staging, and develop branches.
A scripts/setup.sh and .python-version file are generated.
Governance files README.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and Apache 2.0 LICENSE are generated.

evals.prompt: I want to create an agnostic repository called 'devops-playbooks' with no specific framework. I just need a clean structure with shell scripts, docker compose, Lefthook for pre-commit linting (shellcheck and markdownlint), Git Worktrees enabled with scripts/worktree.sh, GitHub Actions CI to validate scripts, and private repository creation on GitHub. Guide me through the interview and set it up.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the agnostic stack mode, asks any frontier questions, presents the blueprint for approval, scaffolds the directory layout with scripts/ and docs/, creates lefthook.yml, scripts/worktree.sh, ci.yml, governance files, and outlines the `gh repo create --private` command.
expectations: The agent recognizes the custom/agnostic mode and does not force an unwanted JS or Python framework.
The blueprint details the agnostic structure, Lefthook configuration, Git Worktrees workflow, CI workflow, and private GitHub repo intent.
The agent honors the approval gate before creating files.
Lefthook configuration includes hooks for shellcheck and markdownlint.
A worktree helper script scripts/worktree.sh is generated and .worktrees/ is ignored in .gitignore.
Git is initialized on the selected initial branch; the agent asks for a commit-message convention rather than assuming Conventional Commits.

evals.prompt: Initialize a repository that already has AGENTS.md requiring approval before commits and a local commit-generating skill that says commits may be created automatically. I have not chosen which rule should win. We do not use worktrees, and our commit messages follow an existing ticket-ID format rather than Conventional Commits. Show me the plan before changing anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects and cites the actual accessible rules, surfaces the commit-approval conflict and asks the user to resolve it before changing affected governance. It preserves the chosen no-worktree and ticket-ID policies instead of generating mandatory worktree or Conventional Commits instructions.
expectations: The agent does not silently choose between AGENTS.md and the commit skill or assume a named skill exists without finding it.
The blueprint lists each material conflict with source, consequence, and a decision requested from the user.
The generated governance does not require worktrees or Conventional Commits when those policies were rejected.
No external skill or configuration is modified without specific approval.

evals.prompt: Bootstrap an existing GitHub repo on a dedicated branch. Its origin/main has advanced, but fetching origin now fails. I still want a worktree and a PR. Also, my local working tree contains unrelated changes. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: The agent reports that remote freshness is unverified, does not branch from a stale fallback, asks whether offline work is allowed, preserves unrelated changes, and defers push/PR until target divergence can be checked. It does not silently rebase or merge.
expectations: Fetch failure is visible and no fallback silently creates a worktree from an unverified branch.
Unrelated changes are not staged, committed, reset, or cleaned.
The agent does not claim the PR branch is current or publish it without target-branch verification and user authorization.
